tagline: One great lake to the other, by way of Lake Placid.
intro: From Sackets Harbor on Lake Ontario the trail heads inland through Watertown and into the Adirondacks at Natural Bridge, then by Harrisville, Star Lake and Cranberry Lake on to Tupper Lake, Saranac Lake and Lake Placid. From there it runs through Wilmington to Keeseville, just west of Lake Champlain, 170 miles from where it began.

Lake Placid hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1932 and 1980. Keeseville, at the far end, was first called Anderson Falls and grew up on the Ausable River, where one works turned out two tons of horse nails a day.

moments.title: Sackets Harbor
moments.text: In the War of 1812 the Navy's Great Lakes shipyard here put more than 3,000 men to work, and by the fall of 1814 the village was the third-largest place in the state.

moments.title: Natural Bridge
moments.text: In 1812 a hunter crossed the Indian River on what he took for a log, and only when he came back to the same bank did he learn it was a marble arch.

moments.title: Saranac Lake
moments.text: Dr. Edward Trudeau came here in 1876 to treat his own tuberculosis with mountain air, and in 1884 opened a sanitarium that began with one cure cottage called Little Red.
